dialect.detail: Uses screen-oriented DISPLAY/ACCEPT with AT row-column and FOREGROUND-COLOR clauses, INSPECT CONVERTING, and END-IF; consistent with GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus personal/educational use on Windows. Brazilian Portuguese context (CPF, RG, INSS, IRRF fields).
evidence: INSPECT WS-NOME CONVERTING WS-MINUSCULAS TO WS-MAIUSCULAS

purpose.domain_detail: Brazilian payroll calculation: computes gross salary, overtime, INSS (social security) and IRRF (income tax) deductions, and net salary for an employee
purpose.summary: This program implements a Brazilian payroll (folha de pagamento) screen. It accepts employee data (name, registration, CPF, RG, role, admission date, base salary, hours, overtime, dependents), computes INSS and IRRF taxes using Brazilian tax brackets, and displays gross and net salary on a character-mode screen.

notable_features: Screen-oriented DISPLAY/ACCEPT with AT row-column addressing
FOREGROUND-COLOR clause for colored screen output
Brazilian tax bracket logic (INSS and IRRF)
No FILE SECTION files used despite FILE SECTION declared
No PERFORM or CALL statements — purely inline sequential logic
verdict.notes: Author comment in Portuguese ('ADRIANO EU SOU OARIO LIXO') and date 03/11/2016 suggest a student exercise. The screen coordinates (row-column AT clauses) imply a terminal/console environment such as GnuCOBOL with curses or Micro Focus. All PIC clauses use integer types (no COMP-3, no decimals), which may cause rounding issues in real payroll use. No PERFORM or CALL — all logic is flat inline code.
